vignette: 72-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%) and severe functional mitral regurgitation, NYHA class III despite 4 months of stable maximally tolerated GDMT and a CRT device implanted a year ago. No aortic stenosis. The interventional cardiologist and the heart failure cardiologist each independently evaluated the patient face to face, and the heart failure cardiologist documents persistent symptoms despite maximally tolerated GDMT and CRT. The planned mitral TEER system has FDA premarket approval and will be used for its FDA-approved indication. The heart team includes a board-certified cardiac surgeon (35 mitral surgeries per year, 60% repairs), a board-certified interventional cardiologist (120 career structural procedures, 45 trans-septal interventions including 30 as primary operator), a board-certified interventional echocardiographer (40 trans-septal guidance and 80 structural procedures), and an advanced heart failure cardiologist. Each patient's suitability for surgical repair, TEER, or palliative therapy is documented and shared with the team. The interventional cardiologist will perform the TEER with the interventional echocardiographer performing TEE and a separate anesthesiologist providing anesthesia; all have device-specific training. The hospital has on-site valve surgery, interventional cardiology, and a cardiovascular ICU; performs 30 mitral surgeries for severe MR per year (15 repairs); has 3 valve surgeons, 2 interventional cardiologists, and 500 PCIs per year; and participates with the heart team in a national audited TEER registry that meets all of the registry requirements in this NCD.
rationale_note: Functional MR despite 4 months of stable max GDMT plus CRT.
